verdict.rationale: ROS 2 documents its own command-line introspection suite: `ros2` subcommands for nodes, topics, services, echoing live topic messages, retrieving parameters, service introspection, topic statistics and tracing. Together these cover inspecting live topics and some state. The evidence does not explicitly document doing this remotely against a deployed robot or viewing logs; only a community remark says ROS delivers value in multi-machine systems. Missing for 10: explicit remote or cross-machine debugging workflow docs, log inspection/aggregation tooling, hands-on corroboration of debugging a deployed robot.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can inspect live topics, logs, and state on a deployed robot remotely to debug issues

citations.quote: ROS 2 includes a suite of command-line tools for introspecting a ROS 2 system.
The main entry point for the tools is the command ros2, which itself has various sub-commands for introspecting and working with nodes, topics, services, and more.
the topic sub-command can be used to publish and echo messages on a topic.
When you enable topic statistics for a subscription, ROS publishes the collected data at regular intervals as a MetricsMessage on a statistics topic.
trace: Tracing tools to get information on ROS nodes execution (only available on Linux)
